LMP3.title: Graff wins as United clinches LMP3 title
LMP3.dek: Trouillet, Petit and Guibbert won in Graff’s #9 from pole, while second place in United’s #2 gave Brundle, Guasch and England the LMP3 title with a round to spare.

chapters.title: United one result from the title
text: LMP3 arrived at Spa with the championship nearly settled. Brundle, Guasch and England led the standings in United Autosports’ Ligier #2 by 30 points with two rounds left, and a finish ahead of the Duqueine #19 and Graff #9 with a margin of 27 points or more would give them the crown in Belgium. It was the series’ first visit to the circuit since 2011.

The class came with 18 cars, all of them Ligier JS P3 Nissans, after Eurointernational stayed away. The By Speed Factory #5 was run by SPV Racing for the weekend with a late line-up of Rodkjaer, Polley and O’Hara. Oak Racing’s #4 had Peugeot-Citroën chief executive Carlos Tavares sharing with Maris in place of Merlin, and McCaig replaced Warburton in RLR MSport’s #15. United’s #2 headed the first practice session, ahead of Panis Barthez and Yvan Muller Racing; sister car #3 led the second, with the #2 and Graff’s #9 behind.

chapters.title: Graff takes its first pole of the year
text: A frantic final few minutes settled LMP3 qualifying, with the top seven cars covered by just over a second. Guibbert put Graff’s #9 on pole with 2:14.392, the team’s first LMP3 pole of 2016. Bell was 0.064 seconds behind in United’s #3, and Moore took Tockwith’s Ligier #26 to third after coming close to a repeat of his Paul Ricard pole.

Gachet was fourth for Panis Barthez, Brundle fifth in the points-leading #2 and Ehrlacher sixth for Yvan Muller Racing’s M.Racing-YMR car. The #5 SPV entry never set a time, as the team fought braking-system trouble in the garage, and Maris’s Oak #4 was the slowest car that did, on 2:18.602, from 37th on the grid.

chapters.title: Brundle jumps to second
text: Guibbert kept the lead of the class from pole, while Brundle went from fifth to second on the opening lap in the #2. The race was neutralised early, and when it settled down both United cars took the longer mandatory stop at the first opportunity after about an hour. That dropped the #3 to ninth and the #2 to 11th once the cycle was complete, with Guasch, who had taken over the championship leader from Brundle, quickly climbing back towards the top ten.

chapters.title: Laurent leads at the break
text: The Murphy LMP2 crash at Bruxelles brought a safety car, and a second crash at the same place by the Pegasus Morgan stopped the field again just after the half-way mark. By then Thomas Laurent was ahead in the M.Racing-YMR Ligier #18, though Graff’s #9 had led the class for most of the opening two hours.

chapters.title: United recovers, Tockwith loses a podium
text: The long safety-car period compressed the field, and United’s two cars worked their way back to second and third. Tockwith’s Moore and Hanson had looked good for a podium with about 90 minutes left, but a puncture for Hanson sent him off the road and back to the pits, and the #26 eventually finished 12th. Lahaye’s Ultimate #17 started 11th in the class and climbed steadily to fourth. The 360 Racing Ligier #6 made a similar rise to fifth, ahead of Inter Europol’s #13.

chapters.title: Graff holds on
text: Petit, Trouillet and Guibbert brought the #9 home first, with the two United Ligiers behind them. The race ended under a full-course yellow while Pizzitola’s LMP2 Ligier was recovered from the gravel, so the order was frozen as the cars crossed the line. Seven LMP3 cars finished on the winner’s lap, 92 laps in all, four fewer than the overall winner.

chapters.title: United crowned in second place
text: Graff took the win with Petit, Trouillet and Guibbert, while United’s Brundle, Guasch and England finished second in the #2 and that was enough to win the 2016 LMP3 drivers’ title with a round to spare. The team had won the first three races of the season, at Silverstone, Imola and the Red Bull Ring. Brundle said the weekend was a great way to finish the job with a team that produced an excellent car race after race, and Guasch likened the class to European Formula 3 and called the year wonderful.

Bell, Patterson and Boyd completed the podium in the sister #3. Lahaye, Heriau and Lahaye were fourth in the Ultimate #17, ahead of the 360 Racing #6, Inter Europol’s #13 and the second Graff, #10 of Falb, Rayhall and Potolicchio, in seventh. RLR MSport, Villorba Corse and Duqueine’s #20 took eighth to tenth; Panis Barthez’s #16 was 11th and Tockwith’s #26 12th, with Oak’s #24 and #4 next. The M.Racing-YMR #18, Duqueine’s #19, Race Performance’s #8 and the SPV-run #5 were not classified.

Graff was due to stay in the European Le Mans Series in 2017, with a new Oreca 07 and a continued LMP3 programme. The final round, at Estoril in October, now only had the LMP2 and GTE titles to decide.

facts.v: Guibbert’s 2:14.392 gave Graff its first LMP3 pole of 2016.

LMGTE.title: JMW wins again at Spa
LMGTE.dek: Smith, Butcher and Bertolini won in JMW’s Ferrari #66 after Butcher jumped from fourth to first on lap one, with Proton’s Porsche #88 second.

chapters.title: JMW leads a tight GTE title fight
text: Spa was the series’ first visit since 2011, and the GTE title was far from decided. Eight points separated the top three in the standings, with JMW Motorsport’s Bertolini, Smith and Butcher in front. The class had the same eight cars as Le Castellet, and the only line-up changes were Christina Nielsen returning to Formula Racing’s Ferrari #60 and Cairoli to Proton Competition’s Porsche #88.

AT Racing’s Ferrari #56, with Pier Guidi, led the first practice session, with JMW’s Ferrari second and the two Proton Porsches next. Cairoli turned the order around in the second session in the #88, ahead of AF Corse’s #51 and Aston Martin Racing’s #99.

chapters.title: Ferrari’s first GTE pole of 2016
text: Pier Guidi put the AT Racing Ferrari on class pole with 2:17.038, the first time a Ferrari had started a GTE race from the front in 2016. Cairoli was 0.338 seconds slower in the #88 Porsche, having led after the first run of flying laps, and neither driver improved at the end. Pier Guidi said the Proton Porsches looked more aggressive on tyre wear.

Griffin took third for AF Corse in the #55, displacing Bertolini, who put the points-leading JMW Ferrari #66 fourth. Turner was fifth in the Aston Martin #99, ahead of Henzler’s Porsche #77, Cioci’s AF Corse Ferrari #51 and Mac’s Formula Racing Ferrari #60, 2.2 seconds off the pole.

chapters.title: Butcher goes from fourth to first
text: Butcher made the start of the race, taking the JMW Ferrari #66 from fourth to the lead on the opening lap, with the pole-sitting #56 and Cameron’s #55 behind. The #55 fell back after the restart, and the #66 pulled away from the #51 and the #56. Then contact between Krohn’s LMP2 Ligier and the Formula Racing Ferrari #60 on lap 10 brought another full-course yellow and compromised the Ferrari’s race.
On lap 20 the #56 spun, and as the class made its first round of stops the #66 remained in front, with the #51 and Roda’s Porsche #88 behind.

chapters.title: Lead changes at the half
text: The opening two hours saw several lead changes in the class, and Smith was in front for JMW at the break. The two safety cars that followed, for the Murphy and Pegasus crashes at Bruxelles, kept the field close together and gave the strategies a chance to re-sort.

chapters.title: The JMW Ferrari pulls clear
text: JMW made the most of the neutralisations, and the #66 kept control of the class into the final hour. The #88 held second, while the #77 Proton Porsche and Griffin’s #55 fought over the last podium place.

chapters.title: Griffin pips Henzler for third
text: The race ended under a full-course yellow, but the fight for third stayed open until the last moments, when Griffin got the AF Corse Ferrari #55 past Proton’s Porsche #77. JMW took its third straight class win, with Roda, Ried and Cairoli second in the #88.

chapters.title: JMW stretches its title lead
text: Smith, Butcher and Bertolini won in the JMW Ferrari #66, ahead of the Proton Porsche #88 of Roda, Ried and Cairoli and the AF Corse Ferrari #55 of Cameron, Griffin and Scott. The win was the team’s third in a row and extended its lead in the GTE standings, and the fastest lap of the class was Butcher’s 2:20.298. Butcher said that many cars bunched up at the end of the first corner, and that he slipped through and found clear air.

Henzler, Hedlund and Seefried were fourth in Proton’s #77, followed by Aston Martin Racing’s #99 of Howard, Turner and Macdowall, AF Corse’s #51 of Perazzini, Cioci and Aguas, and Formula Racing’s #60 of Laursen, Mac and Nielsen, seventh and last of the classified cars, eight laps behind the JMW Ferrari. Nielsen said that the early contact had left the car out of contention. AT Racing’s polesitting #56 was not classified.
The GTE title, like the LMP2 crown, now goes to the Estoril finale in October.

facts.v: Pier Guidi’s 2:17.038 was the first time a Ferrari started an ELMS GTE race from class pole in 2016.
